fixtures: Files are copied into the run's data/ folder.

evals.name: github-review
evals.prompt: Write my review comments on the change in data/diff.patch, for acme/api#55. The retry keeps sleeping even after ctx is cancelled, which needs fixing. The hard-coded one-second sleep is optional, take it or leave it.
evals.expected_output: Two separate review comments tied to lines of sync/retry.go. The cancellation one says what is wrong, why it matters and gives a fix in a GitHub suggestion block selecting on ctx.Done(). The hard-coded sleep is optional polish and is marked nit:.
assertions: Gives the two findings as separate comments
Ties each comment to a line or location in sync/retry.go
The cancellation comment explains why it matters
Offers the cancellation fix in a GitHub suggestion block (a ```suggestion fence)
Marks the hard-coded sleep comment as nit:

evals.name: email-shape
evals.prompt: Draft a reply to data/customer-email.md. Facts are in data/facts.md.
evals.expected_output: An email reply: greets Priya by first name, answers in the first sentence, then detail, then the next step and who owns it, a short sign-off, and no new subject line because it continues a thread.
assertions: Opens by greeting Priya by first name
The first sentence after the greeting answers whether it is fixed
Names the next step and who owns it
Does not add a new Subject line

evals.name: unclear-platform
evals.prompt: Write a reply to my teammate saying I can't make Thursday's planning session but can do Friday morning.
evals.expected_output: Asks which platform the reply is for (Slack, email or a calendar response) before drafting, or drafts for a platform it names and labels. Either way it does not silently produce a long email.
assertions: Either asks which platform the reply is for before drafting, or labels its draft with the platform it chose
If it drafted a reply, the draft offers Friday morning and is at most three sentences
Does not produce an unlabelled long email
